title: Devissage of a constructible sheaf
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions], and let $F$ be a constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$; constructible and lisse mean [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. There is a finite filtration
by subsheaves
$$
0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F
$$
and locally closed constructible subschemes (immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose images are constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset])
$j_r:X_r\hookrightarrow X$, with
lisse
$\Lambda$-sheaves $L_r$ on $(X_r)_{{\mathrm{et}}}$, such that
$$
F_r/F_{r-1}\cong(j_r)_!L_r\qquad(1\leq r\leq m).
$$
For a locally closed immersion $j_r$, choose its factorization as an open immersion
$u_r:X_r\hookrightarrow\overline X_r$ into its scheme-theoretic closure (the closed subscheme cut out by the kernel of the structure-sheaf restriction to $X_r$) followed by a closed immersion
$i_r:\overline X_r\hookrightarrow X$, and define $(j_r)_!L_r:=(i_r)_*(u_r)_!L_r$, with direct image as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].
Here $(u_r)_!$ is the extension by zero of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] along the open immersion. The filtration need not split.

proof.text: We prove the assertion simultaneously for all finite-type $k$-schemes by induction on dimension, which is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; the empty scheme is the initial case, with $m=0$. For nonempty $X$, apply [fin2-lem-lisse-dense-open] to obtain an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ such that $L=j^{-1}F$ is lisse and the closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ has $\dim Z<\dim X$. The complement $Z$ is again finite type over $k$: intersect a finite affine finite-type cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ with $Z$ to obtain the quotient algebras $B/I$. The coefficient convention is inherited by $Z$, since the image of an invertible $N$ is invertible in every quotient.

For the complementary open and closed immersions, [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] gives the exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_!j^{-1}F\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}F\longrightarrow0.$$

The inverse image $i^{-1}F$ is constructible on $Z$ by [prop-constructible-pullback], applied in the category of $\Lambda$-module sheaves. Apply the induction hypothesis to obtain $0=H_0\subset\cdots\subset H_t=i^{-1}F$ on $Z$, with quotients $(b_s)_*(v_s)_!M_s$, where $v_s:T_s\hookrightarrow C_s$ is open into the closure of its stratum and $b_s:C_s\hookrightarrow Z$ is closed. The statement of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] explicitly asserts that direct image of a closed immersion is exact for the finite ring $\Lambda$. Thus $G_s=i_*H_s$ is a filtration $0=G_0\subset\cdots\subset G_t=i_*i^{-1}F$, and $G_s/G_{s-1}\cong i_*(b_s)_*(v_s)_!M_s$.

We check the locally closed extension notation for these quotients and for $A=j_!L$. For the strata of $Z$, the composite $i b_s:C_s\hookrightarrow X$ is closed: on affine opens the corresponding surjective ring maps compose to a surjective map [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It is the closure of $T_s$ in $X$, since the kernel defining this closure is the inverse image in $\mathcal O_X$ of the kernel defining $C_s$ in $\mathcal O_Z$. By the section formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $i_*(b_s)_*Q=(i b_s)_*Q$: on $W\to X$ both have value $Q(W\times_X C_s)$, with the same restrictions and coefficient actions. Hence every quotient from step 3 has the required form. For the first stratum $U$, let $a:C\hookrightarrow X$ be its closure, $u:U\hookrightarrow C$ its open inclusion, and $w:V=X\setminus C\hookrightarrow X$. Here $C\times_X U=U$, since the kernel defining $C$ restricts to zero on $U$. Apply [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], using its finite-module clause concentrated in degree zero, first along $w$ and then along $a$: since $V\times_XU$ is empty, $w^{-1}A=0$ (the only module sheaf on the empty site is zero); and $a^{-1}A\cong u_!L$. The short exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for the pair $(V,C)$ applied to $A$ therefore gives $A\cong a_*a^{-1}A\cong a_*u_!L$, which is precisely the closure convention in the statement. This argument does not assume that the open supplied in step 1 is dense in every component. The initial stratum $U$ is open in $X$, and a stratum locally closed in the closed subscheme $Z$ is locally closed in $X$: if it is $O\cap D$ in $Z$, write $O=Z\cap O_X$ with $O_X$ open and $D$ closed in $X$. All these locally closed subsets are constructible because $X$ is finite type over a field, hence Noetherian, as recorded in [def-weil-constructible-subset].

proof.text: Let $q:F\twoheadrightarrow i_*i^{-1}F$ be the epimorphism of step 2, whose kernel is $A=j_!L$. Set $F_0=0$ and $F_{s+1}=q^{-1}(G_s)$ for $0\le s\le t$. Then $F_1=A$, $F_{t+1}=F$, and $F_1/F_0=A$. For $1\le s\le t$, restriction of the epimorphism $q$ to the inverse image $q^{-1}(G_s)$ is an epimorphism onto $G_s$; its composite onto $G_s/G_{s-1}$ has kernel $q^{-1}(G_{s-1})=F_s$. The cokernel universal property in an abelian category therefore gives $F_{s+1}/F_s\cong G_s/G_{s-1}$. Step 4 identifies all these factors with extensions from lisse sheaves on locally closed constructible subschemes of $X$, so $m=t+1$ works. If $t=0$, this is just $0\subset A=F$.
